definition: Reports of the meeting of a committee of Congress (Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge) with Lord Howe on Staten Island in September 1776: their setting off, and the committee's report to Congress. Contains those two groups.
label: Staten Island peace conference

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).
definition: Printings of a letter to the settlers on the Watauga and Nolachucky rivers, signed 'Henry Stuart, Deputy Superintendent', for the British superintendent of Indian affairs in the southern district, with a sworn statement that a stranger delivered it on 18 May 1776. The letter invites those 'willing to join his Majesty's forces, as soon as they arrive at the Cherokee nation' to sign a paper of allegiance, and says that the King will land an army in West Florida and march it through the Creek nation to the Chickasaws, 'where 500 warriors from each nation are to join them', and on by the Cherokees, 'who have also promised their assistance'. The papers printed it in June and July as a letter delivered to the frontier inhabitants, and from late August among papers sent from Augusta, Georgia, as 'an intercepted letter'. One side's letter, as printed.
label: Henry Stuart's letter to the frontier inhabitants, May 1776

admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a paragraph of the London Sun of 10 April 1793: it was rumoured that Dumouriez, having found reason to doubt his army's promises to support his plan of marching to Paris and placing young Louis on the throne, had left it at the head of a regiment of cavalry. A rumour, labelled as one. Several papers print it with a New York introduction ('In the Sun, of the 10th April, which is the latest paper received'), the others among London paragraphs.
label: The Sun of 10 April: Dumouriez rumoured to have left his army

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a 'Swedish bulletin' from the headquarters of the Swedish army, April 1806, from London papers: reports 'received from adjutant general count Lowenhielm' said the Prussians had taken several villages near Lauenburg, and on the 23rd 'the Prussians passed the Lauenburg frontier'. One army's own account.
label: A Swedish bulletin: the Prussians cross into Lauenburg

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a New York report (end of July 1776) that about fifteen inhabitants drove off five boats from the men of war trying to land on Tappan meadows.
label: Boats driven off at Tappan

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the report of Littleton W. Tazewell to the Mayor of Norfolk (5 July 1807) on delivering the Mayor's answer on board the Bellona: Douglas said his letter had been misapprehended and that he intended no menace. Includes one shorter account of the report.
label: Tazewell's report to the Mayor

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings of this report, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a Norfolk report, from a passenger on the Danish ship Christian Haven, that the British attack on Santa Cruz de Tenerife (July 1797) was driven off. Other Tenerife accounts in the collection are different texts and are not included.
label: Tenerife defeat report

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the thirtieth bulletin of the French Grand Army, dated Austerlitz, 12 Frimaire, year 14 (3 December 1805): 'The 6th Frimaire, the emperor, upon receiving the communication of the full powers of Messrs. de Stadion and de Giulay, offered previously an armistice'. The French army's official account of the battle.
label: The thirtieth bulletin of the Grand Army

admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round two, 6-paper threshold for 1793).
definition: Printings of a bulletin from the London Gazette, dated Tournai, 3 May 1793: on the 1st the French attacked the advanced posts of the left wing and of the centre of the combined army and were repulsed, with the loss of men and cannon. The British government's own account. Four papers print it after another Tournai paragraph on the preparations against Condé.
label: The London Gazette from Tournai, 3 May: the French attacks repulsed

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: The President's message to the Senate of 10 January 1806 with the French government's complaints against American trade with St. Domingo, and the act of 28 February 1806 that prohibited trade with the parts of the island 'not in possession, and under the acknowledged government of France'. Contains those two groups.
label: Trade with St. Domingo: the French complaints and the act of 28 February 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round two, 6-paper threshold for 1793).
definition: Printings of the circular of the Secretary of the Treasury to the collectors of the customs (Philadelphia, 4 August 1793): as repeated contraventions of neutrality had taken place in American ports, the collectors were to watch for vessels arming or equipping for the powers at war, with the schedule of 'Rules adopted by the President' on arming, equipping and prizes. The circular and its rules are one publication. An official document.
label: Hamilton's circular to the collectors, with the President's rules on neutrality

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the treaty of peace between Austria and France signed at Pressburg on 26 December 1805: 'His majesty the emperor of Germany and Austria, and his majesty the emperor of the French, king of Italy, equally animated with a desire to put an end to the calamities of war'. Some papers printed it with the Emperor Napoleon's act of ratification before it. A treaty.
label: The treaty of Pressburg between Austria and France

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of President Jefferson's message to Congress on the dispute with Tunis, read in the House on 14 April 1806: 'During the blockade of Tripoli by the squadron of the U. S. a small cruiser, under the flag of Tunis, with two prizes' tried to enter the port. The executive's own account.
label: The President's message on Tunis, April 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 passages describing the Two Sisters wreck off Bantry Bay, checked against the scan.
definition: Printed accounts of the Rhode Island ship Two Sisters found wrecked off Bantry Bay in August 1797: a reprinted hand-bill and a summary attributed to the Irish papers. Different wording; the wreck itself is not independently verified.
label: Two Sisters wreck

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a paragraph dated Strasburgh, 17 November 1805, from French papers that reached New York in January 1806: 'The city of Vienna has just opened its gates for the first time to a victorious army. This glory was reserved for Frenchmen.' A report from the French side.
label: Strasburgh, 17 November 1805: Vienna opens its gates

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the Virginia Convention's resolutions of 15 May 1776, which instructed the colony's delegates to propose that Congress declare the colonies free and independent states.
label: Virginia Convention, 15 May 1776

admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the 6-paper threshold for 1793).
definition: Printings of a Philadelphia paragraph of early September 1793: by an express to the War Office from the commissioners for treating with the Indian nations north of the Ohio, they 'were not able even to effect a meeting' with the nations assembled at the rapids of the Miami river; the nations' deputation 'insisted upon the Ohio as the boundary between them and the United States', and, 'as so extensive a concession was inadmissible', the commissioners left on 17 August. It names the Wyandots, Delawares, Shawanese and Miamis as 'determined for war', says that a considerable part of them were for peace, and that the Six Nations, with Captain Brandt (Brant) and his Mohawks, urged peace. The United States government's account, as the papers printed it.
label: The War Office on the treaty commissioners, September 1793

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the account of the interview of 20 July 1776 between General Washington and Colonel Patterson, General Howe's adjutant general.
label: Washington meets Colonel Patterson

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the speech of John Wilkes, Lord Mayor of London, in the House of Commons on the motion for an address to the King at the opening of the session in October 1775, against the war in America.
label: Wilkes's speech in the Commons

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Documents and reports of the charges that General James Wilkinson had taken money from the Spanish government, as the 1808 papers printed them: his challenge to John Randolph and Randolph's answer (December 1807), Daniel Clark's statement to the House, the President's message of 20 January, and the opinion of the military court of inquiry (printed from 4 July). Contains those four groups. The statement and the letters are allegations and each writer's own account; the court found no evidence.
label: Charges against General Wilkinson, 1808

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the opinion of the military court of inquiry at Washington on General Wilkinson (signed by its president, Colonel Burbeck, and approved by the President), printed from 4 July 1808: it found no evidence that Wilkinson had received a pension or money from the Spanish government for corrupt purposes.
label: The court of inquiry's opinion on Wilkinson

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).
definition: Printings of notes exchanged at Baltimore on 26 and 27 October 1808, as published there: General James Wilkinson's note to Captain Robert Goodloe Harper, commanding a company of volunteer artillery, charging that Harper had 'secretly assailed the General's honour' and demanding 'the only admissible atonement'; Harper's refusal, which says that his advice to Mr. Clark to lay before Congress documents on Wilkinson's 'connection with the Spanish government' gave no ground for a challenge; and Wilkinson's reply. Each man's own words. The papers print them under their own introductions or headings, such as 'MODERN CHIVALRY' and '"HECTOR" AGAIN.'
label: General Wilkinson's challenge to Robert Goodloe Harper, October 1808

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an extract of a letter of General Wilkinson, dated Rapids of Red River, 19 September 1806: 'My orders, and the conduct of the Mexicans, are so much at variance'; 'I fear you will be informed blood has been spilt'. The American commander's own account, with his forecast.
label: General Wilkinson's letter from the Rapids of Red River, 19 September

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of two letters of 24 and 25 December 1807, from a pamphlet: General James Wilkinson asks John Randolph, a member of the House, for satisfaction for words injurious to his reputation, and Randolph refuses. Each letter is its writer's own account.
label: Wilkinson's challenge and Randolph's answer

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).
definition: Printings of General Wilkinson's address to the court at New Orleans, as a letter from that city of 18 December 1806 reports it (Washington, 21 January 1807): appearing on a writ of habeas corpus for a man he had arrested, he said he was 'called to account for an act in which I glory', warned that 'the artifices of the confederates' must no longer 'cheat the public judgment' and that 'treason stalks abroad', and spoke of 'the friends of Burr and rebellion'. The report adds that he then charged two lawyers with being parties to the conspiracy. The general's own words, as the letter gives them.
label: General Wilkinson's speech in the court at New Orleans

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: The Marquis de Casa Yrujo, Spain's minister to the United States, and the American government in January 1806: his circular to the other foreign ministers against the President's message, and the letter in which the Secretary of State told him that the President expected his departure, with his answers. Contains those two groups.
label: The Spanish minister Yrujo and the government, 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the circular of the Marquis de Casa Yrujo to the foreign ministers in the United States, dated Philadelphia, 21 January 1806, in a translation from the French: 'The want of correctness which appears to prevail throughout the article, relative to Spain, of the message' of the President. With his note to the Secretary of State. The Spanish minister's own account.
label: Yrujo's circular to the foreign ministers
